validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed -- this is a real, decades-old FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipeline with a public docket history (original certificate CP93-685; expansion CP01-153, 2002; Tuscarora XPress CP20-486, filed June 2020 / in-service Nov 2021) and continuous corporate/press documentation from 1994-1995 through today. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified operating/Gas/transmission -- an interstate natural gas transmission pipeline under FERC jurisdiction, not a gathering/distribution line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row West-operating roster; no relabel/duplicate candidate. The pipeline's FuelSource value 'Gas Transmission Northwest' is NOT a data error/mislabel -- it correctly names the UPSTREAM interconnecting pipeline (roster PID P0231, 'Gas Transmission Northwest,' a wholly separate system) that supplies Tuscarora's gas at Malin, OR; confirmed via tcplus.com ('Tuscarora receives natural gas from its interconnection with the Gas Transmission Northwest, LLC (GTN) pipeline system') and Wikipedia ('connects to Gas Transmission Northwest at Malin, Oregon'). Not a duplicate of P0231 -- Tuscarora is the downstream delivery system, GTN is the upstream supply source; they are correctly two distinct rows. Batch-flagged lead 'TC PipeLines LP is a dissolved entity' as Owner1[100%] -- INVESTIGATED AND REFUTED. TC PipeLines LP did NOT dissolve. On March 3, 2021, TCP was acquired via merger and became 'an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of TC Energy' (tcpipelineslp.com/assetsEXP/tuscarora/, live, dated copyright 2023: 'On March 3, 2021, TC PipeLines, LP completed its previously announced merger with TC Energy... A wholly owned subsidiary of TC Energy has acquired all outstanding common units of TC PipeLines, LP (TCP), and TCP has become an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of TC Energy'). Critically, that same current page still lists 'TCP Ownership 100%' for the Tuscarora asset today, and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscarora_Gas_Pipeline (independent of the TC Energy web family) states 'owned by Tuscarora Gas Transmission Company which in turn is 100% owned by TC PipeLines, LP' in the present tense. So TC PipeLines LP stopped being a PUBLICLY TRADED, SEC-REPORTING entity (delisted from NYSE, its last 10-K covered FY2020) but remains a live legal entity and the direct 100% owner of record of Tuscarora. The sheet's Owner1='TC PipeLines LP'/100% is CORRECT AND CURRENT; the brief's dissolution premise is wrong. VALUE CONFIRMATIONS (all independently corroborated, none previously cited on the sheet -- this cohort has zero filled [ref] cells): Capacity=230.00 MMcf/d -- tcplus.com/Tuscarora ('a design capacity of approximately 230 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)') and the TC Energy Tuscarora XPress Fact Sheet PDF ('has a current capacity of approximately 230 MMcf/d') both state the exact figure; both are TC Energy-family sources (one corporate origin under the strict independence test), so tier=medium. Length=305.00 mi -- tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/tuscarora-transmission-system/ ('The 305-mile (491-km) Tuscarora Gas Transmission System') and tcpipelineslp.com/assetsEXP/tuscarora/ ('Length 305 miles') agree exactly (TC family, one origin), AND independently corroborated in km by GlobalData/offshore-technology.com via Wayback ('The 491km-long Tuscarora gas pipeline... maximum diameter of 20 inches') -- genuinely independent of TC Energy -- so tier=high. Reconciled against three other length figures found in the record: the ORIGINAL 1995 mainline was 229 miles Malin OR to Tracy/Reno NV (California CEQA Draft EIR, SCH#1993112055, received 12/22/1994: 'PROPOSED 229 MILE LONG, 20" DIAMETER NATURAL GAS PIPELINE FROM MALIN, OREGON TO RENO, NEVADA, ALSO [SERVING] ALTURAS, SUS[ANVILLE]...' laterals; Wikipedia and the XPress Fact Sheet PDF both still cite '229 miles' for the historical mainline and 'the 300-mile system, which includes associated laterals' for today's total). The system grew via a 2002 CP01-153 extension (14 miles, to a new Wadsworth, NV terminus, per contemporaneous Power Engineering (2002) trade coverage) plus incremental laterals (Alturas, Susanville, Herlong/Sierra Army Depot, a 1996 Klamath/Siskiyou lateral under CP96-166) to reach today's 305-mile system total -- a well-documented, non-conflicting evolution, not a data error. Location: StartLocation=Malin, OR / EndLocation=Wadsworth, NV -- CONFIRMED CURRENT via tcplus.com ('Originates Near: Malin, OR / Terminates Near: Wadsworth, NV'), tcpipelineslp.com ('Originates near: Malin, Oregon / Terminates near Wadsworth, Nevada') and Wikipedia ('Malin, Oregon and runs 229 miles... to Wadsworth, Nevada'); tier=high (Wikipedia independent of TC family). Historical note for context only (not a defect): the pipeline's ORIGINAL 1995 terminus was near Reno/Tracy, NV per the CEQA Draft EIR and the XPress Fact Sheet PDF ('extends approximately 229 miles southeasterly to its terminus in Storey County, Nevada, at NV Energy's Frank A. Tracy Generating Station'); Wadsworth only became the system terminus after the 2002 CP01-153 extension. StartYear1=1995 -- CONFIRMED via tcplus.com ('Commenced Operations: 1995'), tcpipelineslp.com ('Began operations 1995'), tcenergy.com ('...since it came on stream in 1995'), and Wikipedia ('opened in 1995'); tier=high (Wikipedia independent). Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission -- all confirmed by every source read; no conflicting evidence anywhere. Two harvested wiki citations were checked and found to have ROTTED since the wiki page's last access: the bit.ly/2lhXIzg shortener (Wikipedia redirect) still resolves fine, but https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/tuscarora-xpress-project/ (harvested cite_note-:0-7, wiki accessdate 2021-12-06) now returns a live HTTP 404 -- the XPress project page was removed after the project went in-service in Nov 2021; and https://www.ferc.gov/media/c-3-cp20-486-000-052021 (harvested cite_note-10) 403s on a direct scripted fetch (consistent with FERC's known bot-blocking) and its Wayback snapshot renders only a bare nav shell with no docket text, so the docket's substance could not be independently re-verified through that exact URL within this pass -- not used as a citation below. https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (harvested cite_note-:5-9) is a generic EIA hub page that never names Tuscarora -- correctly excluded as a non-naming ref, consistent with prior batches. All other 6 harvested citations verified live and were used as primary evidence above.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's ProposalYear=1994 (currently MISSING_REF -- no ref, value present) could not be directly confirmed. The earliest primary document located is the California State Lands Commission's Draft EIR for the project, logged under CEQA State Clearinghouse (SCH) Number 1993112055, RECEIVED 12/22/1994 (ceqanet.opr.ca.gov/1993112055/2, verified live 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, url_verifier ok=true name_found=true). California's SCH numbering convention assigns the FIRST FOUR DIGITS as the year a project was first submitted for state environmental review -- so SCH#1993112055 itself asserts a 1993 origin even though this particular Draft EIR document wasn't logged as 'received' until December 1994. Independently, the pipeline's original FERC certificate docket is commonly cited elsewhere (Federal Register historical filings; not independently re-verified live in this pass) as CP93-685 -- FERC's docket-numbering convention encodes the ORIGINAL FILING YEAR as the two digits after 'CP', which for 'CP93-685' is 1993. Two entirely independent formal numbering/reference-ID systems (a state clearinghouse and a federal regulatory docket) both encode 1993, which is suggestive but NOT dispositive -- neither source contains an explicit prose statement such as 'Tuscarora filed its FERC application in 1993.' Given this, I flag it at MEDIUM confidence as a candidate correction (1993 instead of 1994) rather than asserting it as fact. A more conclusive check would pull the FERC eLibrary docket sheet for CP93-685 directly (blocked to scripted fetches in this pass; ferc.gov's docket search returned only a bare nav shell via Wayback) or the original Federal Register Notice of Application for CP93-685. Recommend NOT overwriting ProposalYear without that direct confirmation; staged here as a concern for a future targeted follow-up.

Could not find an explicit 'construction began/completed in <year>' statement for the original mainline. What IS established: the California Draft EIR/EIS for the project was received 12/22/1994 (CEQA SCH#1993112055; ceqanet.opr.ca.gov/1993112055/2) and the pipeline came into service in 1995 per three sources (tcplus.com 'Commenced Operations: 1995'; tcpipelineslp.com 'Began operations 1995'; Wikipedia 'opened in 1995'; tcenergy.com 'since it came on stream in 1995'). This places construction SOMEWHERE in the late-1994-to-1995 window by inference, but inferring StartYear=ConstructionYear risks fabricating a value the sources don't actually state (environmental review completion and physical construction start are not the same event, and could span the 1994/1995 boundary). Per the standing rule against fabricating a number from inference alone, this is left UNRESOLVED rather than filled at 1995. A dated PHMSA construction/as-built record, an original Federal Register 'notice to construct' order for CP93-685, or a contemporaneous 1994-1995 trade-press article giving a construction start date would resolve this; none was located in searches of Power Engineering, Oil & Gas Journal, and general web search (NaturalGasIntel blocked live and not found archived at the needed URL) within this pass's budget.

cross_row_leads.note: P3601 (Tuscarora XPress, a compressor-upgrade expansion of P0275) is directly documented by the TC Energy Tuscarora XPress Fact Sheet PDF (https://www.tcenergy.com/siteassets/pdfs/natural-gas/tuscarora-xpress/tc-tuscarora-xpress-fact-sheet-june-2020.pdf, verified live, HTTP 200): the project 'will increase the capability of Tuscarora's existing facilities to provide firm transportation service of approximately 15,000 dekatherms per day of natural gas from Malin, Oregon to Wadsworth, Nevada,' via 'replacement of a 600-hp compressor unit with a 1,380-hp compressor unit... at Tuscarora's Wadsworth Compressor Station' -- i.e. a compressor-only capacity expansion with NO new pipe length. Project timeline per the same PDF: FERC application filed June 2020; construction slated to begin June 2021; in-service November 2021. This closely matches P3601's worklist values (0 miles of new length, ~15 MMcf/d incremental capacity = ~15,000 Dth/d). Note that the harvested wiki citation for the XPress PROJECT PAGE (https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/tuscarora-xpress-project/) has ROTTED since the wiki's 2021-12-06 access date -- it now returns a live HTTP 404 (the page was removed after the project entered service) -- so P3601's researcher should use the fact-sheet PDF above (still live) rather than that dead project-page URL, and should independently re-verify P3601's own FERC docket (CP20-486) rather than relying on the harvested ferc.gov citation, which 403s to scripted fetches and whose Wayback snapshot is a bare nav shell with no docket text.
